title: prez applies CSS comment grammar to layout.html, so a stray /* ... */ hides a live external reference
body:
`refuse_external` is applied to three theme surfaces -- `theme.css`, `theme.js` and `layout.html` (`opt/prez/crate/crates/artifact/src/theme.rs:201-206`) -- while `strip_comments` implements CSS's comment grammar. In HTML, `/*` and `*/` are ordinary text. **The stripper honours them anyway, so any live reference between a stray `/*` and a later `*/` in `layout.html` is deleted before the scan sees it, and it ships.** MEASURED 2026-09-09 by vc, at the artifact rather than at the source, both arms, one difference: | `layout.html` | result | artifact | | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `x` | REFUSED | -- | | the same line between `

a /* b

` and `

c */ d

` | **BUILDS** | `x` on line 2, live markup | **This is the same class as 0014, 0015 and 0017 -- an instrument narrower than the property it holds -- on the surface none of them looked at.** Those three were about CSS spellings; this one is about applying CSS's grammar to a language that does not have it. **The over-refusal direction is real too and is the lesser half.** A `theme.js` carrying `// see http://example.com` is refused today, and an HTML attribution in `` is refused, because neither comment form is understood. That is the exact harm the comment exemption exists to prevent, but it fails loudly. The bypass above fails silently. **Population is zero: the estate holds nine `theme.css` files and no `theme.js` or `layout.html` at all**, so no artifact in the wild is affected. The path is nonetheless documented -- prez's own refusal at `theme.rs:435` reads *"a theme directory needs theme.css; theme.js and layout.html are optional"* -- so this is reachable by a supported route and is not hypothetical. **How it was nearly missed, which is worth as much as the finding.** vc measured five cases across both non-CSS surfaces, all five agreed that the mismatch over-refuses, and the ruling was about to be *"a usability defect on an empty population, safe to defer."* The sixth case -- built to attack the hypothesis rather than to confirm it -- reversed it. Five agreeing samples of a wrong model, which is ST0017 design.md 1.14 landing on its own author one section later. Fix is not this issue's to choose; AC-3.13 holds the decision.
